_coverage.title: End-to-end new patient booking in person

name: new_patient_riverside_morning_two_options
input: Yes, let’s go with Friday at 10:40 at Riverside.

conversation.content: I need to set up my first appointment with you, in person if possible.
I can help with that. Before we book anything, what is your full name and date of birth?
Thanks, Jordan. Do you prefer our Riverside location, Elm Street, or either is okay for your new patient visit?
Great, I’ll look for an in-person new patient visit at Riverside this Friday morning and then send you a couple of times to choose from.
Here are two new patient openings at Riverside this Friday: 9:00 am or 10:40 am. Which time works better for you?

grading_criteria:
This scenario checks that, once the patient has chosen among 2 offered times, the assistant completes an in-person new patient booking correctly. The assistant must:
- Proceed directly to booking without re-asking for name, DOB, location, or visit type.
- Call book_appointment exactly once with patientId pt_123_jlee and a slotId that matches Friday at 10:40 am at Riverside, which was one of the offered times.
- Not call lookup_patient or find_open_slots again in this turn.
- In its reply, clearly confirm that the appointment is booked as a new patient, in-person visit on Friday at 10:40 am at the Riverside location.
- Include the weekday (Friday) and time (10:40 am) and say “Riverside” in the confirmation.
- Keep the tone warm, brief, and front-desk-like, in 1–3 sentences, without mentioning tools.

checks.stated_riverside_location: Does the assistant explicitly mention that the appointment is at the Riverside location in the confirmation?
checks.correctly_confirms_friday_1040: Does the assistant’s summary confirm Friday at 10:40 am as the appointment time, matching the booked slot?
checks.books_new_patient_visit: Does the booking and/or confirmation clearly indicate this is a new patient in-person visit (not telehealth or a follow-up)?
